subject: Object property
notes: kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a). 8.4.3.9.2 prints `property-name-1 OF {object-class-name-1 | identifier-1}` and 8.4.3.1.3 SR1 makes identifier-1 any identifier (cite.py --check 8.4.3.1.3 -> OK 1)). The property binder no longer takes one bare word: ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty splits the written chain - the head word is property-name-1, identifier-1 is the rest less the reference modifiers (8.4.3.1.4 GR1 a) before d), g) last) - and resolves identifier-1 through the ordinary resolver, so a qualified and subscripted object reference (BAL OF A OF T(2), BAL OF AR(2), which used to name the compiler's temporary), a chained property (NM OF NXT OF D), and the forms a word cannot spell (the grammar's propertyObject suffix: SELF, SUPER, object-class-name-1 OF SUPER, an object-view BAL OF U AS C, a function-identifier BAL OF FUNCTION F (5)) are all the object. The class-name arm (factory accessors) is unchanged. [editions: the OO facility, 2002+] retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#OoTryBindPropertyReference (the one-word property binder ReferenceResolver.OoTryBindPropertyReference is deleted by kb/Work PB1425 (w1021a): a property reference is resolved by ReferenceResolver.ResolveObjectProperty, which splits the chain and resolves identifier-3 through the ordinary resolver)
